options.B: Any person, regardless of audit-related experience or qualification, who happens to read the audit file
options.C: An individual who has practical audit experience and a reasonable understanding of audit processes, SAs and applicable legal/regulatory requirements, the business environment, and auditing and financial reporting issues relevant to the entity's industry

subject: Auditing and Ethics
question_html: An auditor, after more than six months had elapsed since the audit report was issued, hurriedly assembled the audit file upon receiving a regulator's request and inserted additional papers bearing the current date. What is the concern with this practice?

options.A: There is no concern, since SA 230 permits documentation to be added at any time before it is shared with a regulator, provided the current date is used
options.B: It shows that part of the audit documentation was prepared afterwards, which is not permissible and puts a question mark on the quality of the audit, in addition to breaching the requirement to assemble the final audit file on a timely basis (ordinarily within 60 days of the auditor's report)
options.C: The only concern is that the papers were dated incorrectly; had they been backdated to the original report date instead, this would have been fully compliant
options.D: There is no concern, since the regulator's request itself extends the permissible timeline for assembling the audit file indefinitely

answer_html:
B. It shows that part of the audit documentation was prepared afterwards, which is not permissible and puts a question mark on the quality of the audit, in addition to breaching the requirement to assemble the final audit file on a timely basis (ordinarily within 60 days of the auditor's report)

Assembling the audit file more than six months after the report (well beyond the ordinary 60-day limit) and inserting papers prepared afterwards - even if honestly dated - shows part of the documentation was prepared later, which is impermissible and casts doubt on audit quality; backdating would have compounded, not cured, the problem.
